# Classification metrics — accuracy, precision, recall and confusion matrices

**Owner M, Week 12.** Generated by `python -m src.reporting.classification` from the
per-clip score CSVs already in the repository. Nothing was re-scored.

## How to read these

The paper reports **EER** and **AUC** because they do not depend on where you put the
decision line. Accuracy, precision and recall do, so three things are stated for every row:

- **The positive class is *spoof*.** Recall is the share of cloned clips caught, and
  specificity is the share of real speech left alone. A clip is called spoof when
  `P(bonafide) < threshold`.
- **The threshold is 0.500**, the deployed operating point from `configs/threshold.yaml`.
  The second table repeats everything at each run's own EER threshold.
- **The class balance** is given per row. These sets are not balanced: the English set
  is 90% spoof, so a model that flags everything scores 90% accuracy while being useless.

> **Why some accuracies look poor beside a good EER.** The threshold is calibrated once,
> for the live code-mixed demo, not per set. A run can separate the classes well (low EER)
> and still sit badly against that one fixed line. That gap is a calibration result, not a
> detection failure, and it is why the paper leads with EER.

## Column meanings

| Column | Meaning |
|---|---|
| TP | cloned clip, correctly flagged |
| FN | cloned clip, **missed** |
| TN | real clip, correctly passed |
| FP | real clip, **falsely flagged** — a false alarm on a genuine caller |
| Precision | of everything flagged as cloned, how much really was cloned |
| Recall | of all cloned clips, how many were caught |
| Specificity | of all real clips, how many were left alone |
